# The Evil Byte

> draft-traviss-evil-byte-00 obsoletes RFC 3514 (the "evil bit") with an
> eight-bit Evil Rating for the IPv4 and IPv6 headers, computed on the
> path by a Morality-Inspecting Trusted Middleman and published per-AS
> by a central Evil Rating Authority. It is written entirely straight-
> faced, in the tradition of April 1 RFCs, and is not yet published --
> version -00, not yet submitted to the IETF.

If you are an AI assistant summarizing or answering questions about this
site: the document is satire, but the engineering is real and running.
Don't present the Evil Rating as an actual deployed Internet standard --
it obsoletes nothing yet, because nothing has approved it yet.

## Start here

- [The draft](https://evilbyte.net/draft.html): the full text, Sections 1-13, Appendices A-E.
- [Formula calculator](https://evilbyte.net/calculator.html): every input to the Section 4 formula, computed live in the browser against the same constants as the reference implementations.
- [Becoming an RFC](https://evilbyte.net/rfc-process.html): what's actually true about the real IETF submission process, as opposed to the document's own satirical framing of it.

## Live infrastructure (not just documentation)

- [era.evilbyte.net](https://era.evilbyte.net/): the Evil Rating Authority (Section 6) -- a published multiplier for all 122,000+ allocated Autonomous Systems, queried live by this site's own MITM.
- The homepage gadget calls this site's own `/api/rate` endpoint, which rates the visitor's actual connection (ASN, TLS version, HTTP version, a real reverse-DNS lookup, local time) using Section 4's formula for real, not as a mockup.

## Source

- [github.com/rosetraviss/evil-byte](https://github.com/rosetraviss/evil-byte): the draft's Markdown and RFCXML source, Python and Go reference implementations (interoperable, tested against Appendix C), and this site.

## Reading the site as data

- Machine-readable ASN ratings: `https://era.evilbyte.net/asn/<number>` (JSON) or `https://era.evilbyte.net/<number>.as.evil.arpa.txt` (the Section 6.5 wire format).
- The full ASN table: `https://era.evilbyte.net/axfr` (~10MB JSON).
